headline: Experts told Dialogue Earth that Chinese AI weather models are fast and cheap but still struggle to forecast the most extreme storms.
score_reason: Pool score kept: informative explainer, but background rather than a new development.
importance_line: Countries with few weather stations may gain cheap forecasting, but experts say these models underestimate record-breaking events, are hard to explain, and lack agreed verification standards.
summary: Eco-Business, republishing an expert-interview feature by Dialogue Earth, reports that Chinese AI forecasting models such as Fengwu, Pangu-Weather and Fuxi run in minutes on a fraction of the computing power of conventional forecasts. The experts say the models still miss extreme rainfall, as in the 2025 Gansu flash flood that killed 32 people, and that verification standards are lacking.
notes: Feature rests on Dialogue Earth interviews; url is the Eco-Business copy.
